description: A stereo spring reverb built as two spring tanks, each a delay line run through a chain of all-pass coils and fed back on itself

params.text: Sets how hard the signal is pushed into the springs, from silence to three times, with the feedback loop soft-clipping what comes back
Sets how much of the spring's output is fed back into it, up to 1.2; past 1 the tank rings on by itself
Crossfades between the dry signal and the springs, dry at one end and springs alone at the other
Sets the all-pass coefficient of every coil, from 0.05 to 0.95, which is what makes the spring sound tight or slack and shifts the pitch of the twang
Sets the length of the spring in milliseconds, from 10 to 160, which is the time round the loop
Sets the corner of the low-pass filter inside the loop, from 100Hz to 10000Hz, so that each pass loses more or less of the top
Scales the delay spacing between one coil and the next, from 0.05 to 4 times the standard spacing

inputs.text: One side of the stereo pair to be reverberated; with only one input patched it feeds both springs
One side of the stereo pair to be reverberated; with only one input patched it feeds both springs
Adds to the drive, a third of a unit per volt, with the total clamped between 0 and 3
Adds to the reflection, 0.12 per volt, with the total clamped between 0 and 1.2
Adds to the dry-to-spring mix, a tenth per volt, with the total clamped between dry and springs alone
Adds to the tension, a tenth per volt, with the total clamped between 0.05 and 0.95
Adds to the spring length, 15ms per volt, with the total clamped between 10ms and 160ms
Moves the damping corner an octave per volt, with the result clamped between 20Hz and 10000Hz
Moves the coil spacing, 0.4 per volt, with the total clamped between 0.05 and 4

outputs.text: That side of the pair, dry and springs mixed according to the MIX controls
That side of the pair, dry and springs mixed according to the MIX controls

notes: the two springs are not identical: the right one is given 2 per cent less tension and a 3 per cent longer length, which is what makes the reverb sound wide from a mono source.
the REFL knob starts at 0.85 and the MIX knob starts fully wet, so a fresh module is all spring and no dry signal.
mono per side: a polyphonic cable is read as its first channel.
the tension and spacing controls are re-read only every 32 samples, so sweeping either with an audio-rate signal will step rather than glide.
the number of coils is saved with the patch, and Rack's randomise picks one of the four settings.
each of the large knobs draws a gold arc from its own position round to where its CV jack has moved it.
menu: Few coils — runs each spring through six all-pass coils, the thinnest and cheapest setting
Mid coils — runs each spring through nine all-pass coils, which is where the module starts
More coils — runs each spring through twelve all-pass coils
Many coils — runs each spring through twenty-four all-pass coils, the densest and most expensive setting
Legacy Mode (Delay) — sets every coil's delay to zero, which is how the module behaved before the coil delays were added; it is switched on for any patch saved before that change
